A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable, complete 34-page versions of the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original length-prediction experiments, scheduling measurements and ablations in Section 4, with additional experiments and GRPO training curves in Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices D–E, including prediction accuracy, system performance, ablations and training curves.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same entropy-guided pooling, soft-label prediction head, combined cross-entropy/MSE objective and progressive length prediction procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same LMSYS and ForeLen coverage, including long-sequence, reasoning and RL sampling tasks. The writingprompts extreme-length evaluation in Appendix E.2 is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SSJF-Reg, SSJF-MC, S3, PiA, TPV, TRAIL and LTR-C. Comparator membership in the main and appendix experiments, including pooling and loss alternatives, is unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported splits, sample counts, prompts, model configurations, metrics and experimental procedures are unchanged. Both retain grouped RL sampling with K=4, the same predictor-training settings and the vLLM/SJF system evaluation.

E4.justification: Both retain the entropy–importance analysis, pooling ablation, loss-weight and loss-function analyses, layer-selection study, extreme-length generalization test and computational-efficiency analysis. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: The stated random seed of 42 and the uncertainty quantities reported with ± in Appendix Tables 6–10 are unchanged. There are no additions or revisions to run-count information, uncertainty estimation or statistical testing.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and plotted results in Tables 1–15 and Figures 1–13 match. For example, Table 1 retains EGTP's Qwen2.5-7B average MAE of 103.47, and Table 2 retains Long Sequence throughput of 131.05.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(9) and the metric definitions in Appendix B are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added, removed or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same EGTP, PLP and ForeLen contributions and accuracy/throughput claims, including the claimed 29.16% MAE reduction.

C2.justification: Interpretations of entropy as a length signal, progressive refinement, generalization and computational efficiency remain identical. No substantive limitations or applicability qualifications change.

D1.justification: Implementation descriptions, hyperparameters, hardware specifications, dataset details and system prompts remain unchanged. The reproducibility statement retains the same code and dataset access links.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the reference list are unchanged. The positioning relative to serving optimizations, auxiliary length predictors and RL sampling remains the same.

P1.justification: The author block changes Yubin Chen's affiliation from MBZUAI to PRADA and Lijie Hu's from BUPT to MBZUAI. The BUPT affiliation line and correspondence footnote are removed, and the version/date stamp changes. Scientific prose and section ordering are unchanged.

P2.justification: The shortened front matter and removed footnote produce limited text reflow and spacing changes across pages 1–4. Figures and tables are unchanged; pages 5–34 render identically.

improvement.justification: v2 makes administrative edits and modest layout changes while preserving all scientific content and evidence, including the appendices. The affiliation changes and removal of the correspondence footnote do not materially alter the paper's scientific quality, clarity or reproducibility.
